{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and found the package to be, on the whole, strongly Customer-favourable. Seventeen of nineteen rules are compliant, including all of the critical-risk IP and indemnity positions: Vendor gives a full defend/indemnify/hold-harmless covenant with Customer-protective settlement consent (§ 20), Customer owns Deliverables and Customer Data with a present assignment and a perpetual paid-up licence to embedded Vendor Technology (§§ 13–14), and assignment, licence scope, termination for convenience, audit, renewal, transition, warranty and insurance all meet the preferred position.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory as drafted:

1. **Limitation of liability cap basis (§ 21).** The architecture is sound — the cap and the damages exclusion are mutual and all seven preferred carve-outs appear in the Excluded Claims definition — but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee only. That makes the cap illusory and far below six months' fees. We have reset the basis to the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, and restated the payment carve-out, which was keyed to the same narrow noun.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay is an uncapped, compounding penalty on a minor breach that can exceed remaining contract value. It is not an early-termination fee and is not capped at three months' fees, so it fails both the preferred and the fallback position. We propose deletion, replaced with a confirmation that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.

No other Customer-payable penalty, exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation exists; several provisions (§§ 7.6, 12.4, 22.3, 24.4) run in our favour and are left untouched.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** (redline repaired) | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Walk-away items

Both open deviations were assessed as walk-away territory and should not be conceded without escalation:

- **§ 21 — cap tied to the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee.** A cap keyed to the § 1.5 definition of "Fees" is illusory and far below six months' fees. We require the reset basis (greater of trailing twelve months' fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms, and USD 1,000,000) and the conforming payment carve-out.
- **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** An uncapped, compounding fifteen percent of annual Fees per week triggered by a ten-day payment delay fails the fallback (no early-termination-fee character, no three-month cap) and must be deleted.

---

## Next steps

1. Send the two redlines to Vendor: the § 21 cap-basis and carve-out reset, and deletion of § 7.7 with a confirmation that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.
2. Raise as a negotiation-only point that § 1.5 still defines "Fees" narrowly; the express scope language and the USD 1,000,000 floor make the cap meaningful on any reading, but aligning § 1.5 would be cleaner.
3. Record the following as noted-not-flagged, for awareness rather than redline: § 14.1's processing right extends to "secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" (constrained by § 15.1); § 19.2's Deliverable conformance period is 90 days rather than twelve months and the malicious-code warranty is limited to code intentionally introduced by Vendor; § 11.2's 30-day data-return clock runs from Customer's request; § 24.2's competitor prohibition is consent-gated rather than absolute; and § 28.3's mutual executive escalation, which does not delay urgent relief.
4. Confirm with the business that the once-per-twelve-months audit mechanic (§ 22) and the six-month transition window at expiring-Order-Form rates (§ 11) match operational expectations.
5. On Vendor's response, we will re-verify §§ 7 and 21 and circulate a short closing note before signature."}
